notes (all optional, with my triage of the built-in findings):
- Provider package left behind (`pi-install.ts:19`): `MANAGED_NAMES` leaves out the provider-profile package. After `pi.provider` changes, setup keeps the old provider package in the settings. The intended behavior says "feature packages", so this is optional.
- Scope mismatch (`pi-install.ts:63`): setup reads one settings file, while doctor accepts either scope. A package already installed at the other scope is installed again, and a removal at one scope leaves the other scope's entry. Optional.
- Git ref with a slash (`pi-check.ts:132`): `sourceName` takes the last path segment, so `git:github.com/o/holyagent@release/0.3.0/integration` is not recognised as the HolyAgent package. The fix command itself uses a `holyagent-<v>` tag, which works. Optional.
- Node floor elsewhere: `install/wsl-install.sh` still accepts Node 22.13, while the Windows installer and the doctor now require 22.19. Docs elsewhere say the same; they are uncommitted and out of scope. Optional.
- Rejected: `pi remove npm:<name>` without the version. Pi's `getSourceMatchKeyForSettings` matches npm sources by name only (`package-manager.js` ~L1195), so the removal works.
- Rejected: setup and doctor run Pi work when `pi` is on PATH. That is the stated intent, and doctor prints one info line otherwise.
- Rejected: `npmCommand` not set by setup. That claim is about the uncommitted docs, which are out of scope.
- Rejected: setup and doctor use the process cwd for `.pi`. Pi resolves `-l` against cwd too, so this is consistent.
- Rejected: `PI_HOST_VERSION` and the pre-release version parse. The pin is guarded by a test, and the point is cosmetic.
- Not run: a real `pi install` or `pi remove`. Everything went through the fake Shell, so end-to-end Pi behavior is read from the code only.

evidence:
- review-findings: the 9 built-in findings are triaged above; 0 blockers, 4 optional notes, 5 rejected with reasons.
- Setup installs exactly the enabled packages at their pins, removes only HolyAgent feature packages the config turns off, and reports failures without aborting the other steps: `pi-install.ts:59-113` filters by `listsAtPin`, removes only `MANAGED_NAMES` that are not wanted, and records each failure as a `failed` line. Tests: `setup-pi.test.ts` "installs every enabled package", "removes a feature package the config turns off", "leaves a package alone", "a failing command is a failed line and the others still run".
- Doctor does not fail a user without Pi and reports each missing or mis-pinned enabled package with its fix command: `pi-check.ts:307-310` returns one `~` info line, `checkFeatures` (`:273-289`) returns one line per missing package with its `pi install` command, and `pi.enable` off adds nothing. Tests: "a machine without Pi gets one informational line", "each enabled package missing", "a package listed at another version is missing".
- Existing setup and doctor behavior for Claude is unchanged: `setup.test.ts` changes are only the added `NOT_IN_USE` line, which is the intended one info line. The Pi step is gated by `!cloud && piInUse`, and the full suite passes.
- Each new behavior has a test that would fail without it: `setup-pi.test.ts` has about 30 behavior tests that assert exact lines and shell calls, covering all new branches (dry run, scope `-l`, cwd, no pi on PATH, bad settings file, cloud, undo).
- The change follows the repository's code rules: lint and type-check pass; there is no try/catch, `new Promise` or async function in the new runtime code. It uses Effect, tagged `SetupFailure`, Schema decode with `onExcessProperty: "error"`, the Shell service and JSDoc on exports. The only fmt failure is the out-of-scope `docs/pi/README.md`.
